types.oie_definition: A specific named motion picture or movie.
types.embedding_query_text: Film Title: A specific named motion picture or movie. Also called Movie, Motion Picture, Film.

chosen_type.label: Movie
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Movie class directly represents a specific named motion picture, matching the OIE type and mentions perfectly.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

types.oie_definition: A Uniform Resource Locator, an address that specifies the location of a resource on the internet.
types.embedding_query_text: URL: A Uniform Resource Locator, an address that specifies the location of a resource on the internet. Also called Web Address, Link, Internet Address.

chosen_type.label: URL
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org URL data type is a direct and precise match for the OIE type and the provided mention.

candidates.label: URL
candidates.comment: A data type representing a Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address. Examples: "https://schema.org", "ftp://example.com/file.zip", "mailto:info@example.com".

candidates.label: BreadcrumbList
candidates.comment: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList representing a hierarchical navigation path, typically on a website, showing the user's current location relative to the site's structure. Also called navigation path, breadcrumbs, site path. Examples: Home > Products > Electronics > Televisions, Blog > Category > Post Title.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: WPFooter
candidates.comment: The bottom section of a web page, typically containing copyright information, contact details, and navigation links. Also called page footer, website footer, site bottom. Examples: the copyright notice at the bottom of a website, links to privacy policy and terms of service, social media icons in the footer.

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

types.oie_definition: A company or institution responsible for gathering and disseminating news and information.
types.embedding_query_text: News Organization: A company or institution responsible for gathering and disseminating news and information. Also called Media Outlet, News Agency, Publisher.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org NewsMediaOrganization class specifically describes organizations that produce and disseminate news, which fits 'latimes.com'.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

types.oie_definition: A specific calendar day, month, or year.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific calendar day, month, or year. Also called Calendar Date, Specific Day, Point in Time.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Date data type is a direct and precise match for the OIE type and the provided mention.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

types.oie_definition: A specific amount of money or currency.
types.embedding_query_text: Monetary Value: A specific amount of money or currency. Also called Currency Amount, Financial Sum, Dollar Amount.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org MonetaryAmount class directly represents a specific amount of money or currency, matching the OIE type and mentions.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

types.oie_definition: A sovereign state or nation.
types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign state or nation. Also called Nation, State, Sovereign State.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Country class directly represents a sovereign state or nation, matching the OIE type and mentions.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

types.oie_definition: A major company involved in the production and distribution of films.
types.embedding_query_text: Film Studio: A major company involved in the production and distribution of films. Also called Movie Studio, Production House, Studio.

chosen_type.label: FilmStudio
chosen_type.definition: A company primarily involved in the production and distribution of films.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class precisely captures a 'Film Studio' as an organization; 'Movie' is a creative work, and other candidates are irrelevant or too specific.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: MovieRentalStore
candidates.comment: A MovieRentalStore is a local business that offers movies for rent. Also called video rental store, film rental shop, DVD rental store. Examples: Blockbuster (historical), local video rental shop, Redbox kiosk. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is a venue for viewing movies.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

types.oie_definition: A specific calendar year.
types.embedding_query_text: Year: A specific calendar year. Also called Calendar Year, Annual Period.

chosen_type.label: CalendarYear
chosen_type.justification: While 'Date' exists, it implies a full date (day, month, year); a specific 'Year' is a distinct concept not directly covered by existing candidates.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.oie_definition: A person who portrays a character in a performance, such as a film or play.
types.embedding_query_text: Actor: A person who portrays a character in a performance, such as a film or play. Also called Performer, Thespian, Player.

chosen_type.label: Actor
chosen_type.definition: A person who portrays a character in a performance.
chosen_type.justification: Existing candidates describe roles or actions, not the person (actor) themselves; a new type inheriting from 'Person' is needed.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: PerformAction
candidates.comment: A PerformAction, as a PlayAction, is the act of participating in performance arts. Also called act, perform, stage. Examples: performing in a play, playing a musical instrument on stage, dancing in a ballet. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader category for engaging in recreational activities.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsTheater
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsTheater is a civic structure or venue for performing arts. Also called theater, playhouse, concert hall. Examples: Sydney Opera House, a local community theater, a Broadway theater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

types.oie_definition: A company that handles the business and logistical aspects of creating films, television shows, or other media.
types.embedding_query_text: Production Company: A company that handles the business and logistical aspects of creating films, television shows, or other media. Also called Production House, Media Producer, Film Company.

chosen_type.label: ProductionCompany
chosen_type.definition: A company that handles the business and logistical aspects of creating media.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class precisely captures a 'Production Company' as an organization; 'EntertainmentBusiness' is too specific (LocalBusiness) and focuses on services rather than production.

candidates.label: Movie

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

candidates.label: TVSeries
candidates.comment: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

types.oie_definition: A person who controls the artistic and dramatic aspects of a film and guides the technical crew and actors.
types.embedding_query_text: Film Director: A person who controls the artistic and dramatic aspects of a film and guides the technical crew and actors. Also called Movie Director, Director, Filmmaker.

chosen_type.label: FilmDirector
chosen_type.definition: A person who controls the artistic and dramatic aspects of a film and guides the technical crew and actors.
chosen_type.justification: Existing candidates are irrelevant to a person's role; a new type inheriting from 'Person' is needed to represent a film director.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

candidates.label: Clip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a larger audio or video program. Also called segment, excerpt, snippet, short video. Examples: A news clip, a movie trailer, a highlight reel from a sports game, a sound bite. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is the broader category for any creative content.

types.oie_definition: A specified period of time with a defined start and end.
types.embedding_query_text: Date Range: A specified period of time with a defined start and end. Also called Time Span, Period, Interval of Dates.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Duration class represents a period of time, which aligns with the concept of a date range, even if the examples are ISO 8601.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.oie_definition: A company specializing in the production of animated films, television shows, or other media.
types.embedding_query_text: Animation Studio: A company specializing in the production of animated films, television shows, or other media. Also called Cartoon Studio, Animation House, Animated Film Company.

chosen_type.label: AnimationStudio
chosen_type.definition: A company specializing in the production of animated films, television shows, or other media.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class precisely captures an 'Animation Studio' as an organization; 'EntertainmentBusiness' is too specific (LocalBusiness) and focuses on services rather than production.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

candidates.label: AdultEntertainment
candidates.comment: AdultEntertainment is an EntertainmentBusiness specializing in content or services intended for adults. Also called adult venue, adult club, adult establishment. Examples: A strip club, an adult movie theater, an adult bookstore.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.oie_definition: A business that specializes in collecting, processing, and analyzing data to provide insights.
types.embedding_query_text: Data Analytics Company: A business that specializes in collecting, processing, and analyzing data to provide insights. Also called Analytics Firm, Data Science Company, Market Research Firm.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: A data analytics company's core function of analyzing data to provide insights aligns well with the definition of a 'ResearchOrganization'.

candidates.label: DataCatalog
candidates.comment: A DataCatalog is a collection or repository of datasets, often providing metadata and access information for each. Also called data repository, dataset collection, data portal. Examples: A government open data portal, a university research data catalog, a scientific data archive.

candidates.label: Dataset
candidates.comment: A Dataset is a structured collection of information or data, typically organized for analysis or use. Also called data collection, data compilation, data repository. Examples: A spreadsheet of sales figures, a database of customer information, a collection of scientific measurements. Distinct from DataCatalog, which is a collection of multiple datasets.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: OnlineBusiness
candidates.comment: An OnlineBusiness is a particular business that operates primarily or entirely online. Also called e-business, internet business, digital enterprise. Examples: an e-commerce site, an online travel agency, a virtual doctor's office. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which has a physical presence.

candidates.label: BusinessFunction
candidates.comment: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.

types.oie_definition: A specific department or subsidiary within a larger film studio organization.
types.embedding_query_text: Film Studio Division: A specific department or subsidiary within a larger film studio organization. Also called Studio Unit, Motion Picture Division, Film Arm.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationalDivision
chosen_type.definition: A specific department or subsidiary within a larger organization.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org class represents an organizational division; a new, reusable type inheriting from 'Organization' is appropriate.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

types.oie_definition: A person holding a senior management position in a business or corporation.
types.embedding_query_text: Business Executive: A person holding a senior management position in a business or corporation. Also called Executive, Corporate Leader, Manager.

chosen_type.label: BusinessExecutive
chosen_type.definition: A person holding a senior management position in a business or corporation.
chosen_type.justification: Existing candidates describe roles or organizational types, not the person (executive) themselves; a new type inheriting from 'Person' is needed.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: BusinessFunction
candidates.comment: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.
